question_text: If the total deviation produced by two plane mirrors is $300^\circ$, then the number of images formed of an object placed symmetrically between them is
solution: The deviation produced by two plane mirrors inclined at an angle $\theta$ is $\delta = 360^\circ - 2\theta$. Given $\delta = 300^\circ$, we have $2\theta = 60^\circ \implies \theta = 30^\circ$. The number of images is $n = \frac{360^\circ}{\theta} - 1 = \frac{360^\circ}{30^\circ} - 1 = 11$.

question_text: A man runs towards a stationary plane mirror with a velocity of $15\text{ m/s}$. The magnitude of the velocity of the man relative to his image is
solution: Taking the direction towards the mirror as positive, $\vec{v}_m = 15\hat{i}\text{ m/s}$ and the image moves with $\vec{v}_i = -15\hat{i}\text{ m/s}$. The relative velocity is $\vec{v}_{m/i} = \vec{v}_m - \vec{v}_i = 15 - (-15) = 30\text{ m/s}$.

question_text: The size of the image formed by a convex lens is one-fourth the size of a real object. If the focal length of the lens is $30\text{ cm}$, then the distance of the object from the lens is
solution: For a real object, a diminished image by a convex lens is real and inverted, so $m = -\frac{1}{4}$. Using $m = \frac{f}{f+u} \implies -\frac{1}{4} = \frac{30}{30+u} \implies 30+u = -120 \implies u = -150\text{ cm}$, giving an object distance of $150\text{ cm}$.

question_text: The refractive index of the material of an equilateral prism is $\sqrt{2}$. The angle of incidence for minimum deviation is
solution: For an equilateral prism, $A = 60^\circ$. At minimum deviation, $r = \frac{A}{2} = 30^\circ$. By Snell's law, $\mu = \frac{\sin i}{\sin r} \implies \sqrt{2} = \frac{\sin i}{\sin 30^\circ} \implies \sin i = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \implies i = 45^\circ$.

question_text: A concave lens is made of three layers of glass of three different materials as shown in the figure. A point object is placed on its axis. The number of images of the object formed is
diagram_description: A biconcave lens sliced vertically into three sections along its thickness, each section composed of a different transparent material.
solution: Because the layers are arranged sequentially along the principal axis, every incident ray from the object traverses all three media in series. The combination acts as a single composite lens with one effective focal length, forming only 1 image.

question_text: A point object $O$ is placed on the principal axis of a convex lens of focal length $f = 20\text{ cm}$ at a distance of $40\text{ cm}$ to the left of it. The diameter of the lens is $10\text{ cm}$. An eye is placed $60\text{ cm}$ to the right of the lens and at a distance $h$ below the principal axis. The maximum value of $h$ to see the image is
solution: With $u = -40\text{ cm}$ and $f = 20\text{ cm}$, the image is formed at $v = +40\text{ cm}$ on the axis. The eye is at $x = 60\text{ cm}$, which is $20\text{ cm}$ past the real image. By similar triangles from the aperture radius $R = 5\text{ cm}$ to the image: $\frac{h_{\max}}{60 - 40} = \frac{R}{40} \implies h_{\max} = 5 \times \frac{20}{40} = 2.5\text{ cm}$.
